newsitem.title: USA: Clark sees Ill. unit back onstream Tues after fire.
newsitem.headline: Clark sees Ill. unit back onstream Tues after fire.

text.p: Clark Refining & Marketing Inc said Monday that a propane unit at its 80,000 barrel-a-day Blue Island, Illinois refinery which had a fire on Saturday would likely be back onstream on Tuesday.
The unit, a propane scrubber, had an explosion early Saturday that halted produciton of about 1,000 barrels a day of propane, according to Syd Wiley, the plant's spokesman.
"We've been working round the clock on it and expect it up no later than tomorrow," he said. Meanwhile, distribution to clients would be met out of storage and would not be disrupted, he said.
He said the company was still looking into the cause of the explosion, which caused no injuries and was unrelated to two mishaps over the previous 18 months, one of which killed two workers.
The plant mostly produces gasoline, production of which was unaffected by Saturday's explosion, Wiley said.
Clark Refining & Marketing Inc is a unit of Clark USA Inc which is 46 pct owned by The Horsham Corp of Canada.
